name: Complementarianism
summary: Complementarianism is the view, coined in 1988 and set out in the Danvers Statement, that men and women are equal in worth and dignity before God but have different, God-ordained roles. In marriage the husband is the head, with primary responsibility for loving, servant leadership, and the wife honours and supports that leadership; in the church some teaching and governing offices are reserved for men. Its texts rest these differences on the created order and Scripture's authority, and reject egalitarian and feminist alternatives. They say little about law, economics or foreign affairs.

tried.how: fetched the page address; it refused scripted access
searched for an encyclopedia or scholarly entry on the term; results were advocacy essays and mirrors

scope: The theological view of gender roles that the Danvers Statement (1988) summarises and Piper and Grudem's 'Recovering Biblical Manhood and Womanhood' (1991) argues, as the Council on Biblical Manhood and Womanhood's own history and complementarian accounts (Burk, FIEC) describe it: equal dignity, distinct created roles, male headship in the home and male eldership in the church. It excludes egalitarianism, and the stricter 'biblical patriarchy' movement. As Burk notes, Danvers does not spell out wider cultural or legal implications, so questions of law and public policy are left unanswered unless the texts speak to them.

authors.quote: Wayne Grudem, one of the key members of the group
